transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-04-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sarah Park (Harbor - Head of Security), Tom Nguyen (Harbor - CISO), Priya Das (Harbor - Compliance), Asha Mehta (Harbor - Platform)
---
Summary (auto): quick run through of SOC2/ISO artifacts, Trust Center access, RBAC/SSO controls, audit logs retention, BYOK/KMS ask, and controls mapping next steps.
Links referenced: Trust Center (redwood): https://console.redwood.ai/trust-center , controls spreadsheet placeholder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/harbor-redwood
---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'll do a quick intro — Maya Chen, AE on the account. Liam from our SE team is with me.
[00:14] Liam: Hi all. I'll focus on the technical posture questions and controls mapping.
[00:23] Sarah: Thanks, um, quick context — Harbor is preparing our vendor evidence pack for an upcoming audit. We're looking to validate Redwood's SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 posture, plus understand how RBAC, SSO, and logging map to our controls.
[00:40] Tom: Timeline is tight, internal audit window middle of May, so we need artifacts and a mapping table by end of April ideally.
[00:53] Maya: Great, we'll do our best. Today we'll show where reports live, what we can share, and plan a controls mapping deliverable.
[01:10] Liam: Quick note — our Trust Center has the certs and scoped reports. For SOC 2 we typically share a redacted Type II report and a controls matrix. For ISO 27001 we provide the certificate and scope statement.
[01:30] Priya: When you say redacted, what gets redacted?
[01:35] Liam: Usually vendor-specific customer data and any third-party contract clauses; the security controls evidence and test results stay. We can provide a cover letter explaining redactions.
[01:49] Asha: Are the reports downloadable from the Trust Center? Or do we get them via S3 link/email?
[01:56] Maya: They are downloadable from the Trust Center once you've been granted access. We can also push them to a secure link. Access is SSO-enabled.
[02:10] Sarah: Do we need a separate account? Our compliance team prefers service accounts for evidence access.
[02:18] Liam: We support SAML-based SSO — you can provision group-scoped access and a service account. RBAC supports read-only Trust Center role.
[02:28] Tom: OK good. Data residency — Harbor needs assurances about EU-only processing for EU-subject data. How are regions and residency enforced?
[02:39] Liam: We have regional execution zones. For hosted customers you can pin processing to a region. For stricter requirements we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) — that gives you control of network egress.
[02:53] Sarah: We're evaluating hosted with strict routing vs Private. Can you map controls that differ between hosted and private?
[03:02] Liam: Yep, controls mapping will include columns for hosted vs dedicated vs private, and indicate where compensating controls apply.
[03:12] Priya: Audit logs — retention and structure? We need immutable logs for 7 years for certain controls.
[03:20] Liam: Our default audit log retention in hosted is 1 year; extended retention is an add-on. For Private you control retention via your SIEM / logging stack. Logs are tamper-evident and we can provide logs via secure export.
[03:35] Sarah: Are logs hashed or signed?
[03:38] Liam: We use write-once append stores and support log signing for dedicated customers — I'll confirm the exact hashing algorithm we use, might be SHA-256, and note whether timestamping uses an external TSA.
[03:52] (background: keyboard clacking)
[04:10] Tom: KMS — critical for us. We need BYOK and HSM-backed keys. What's supported?
[04:18] Liam: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS integrations. For hosted we integrate with customer KMS providers (e.g., AWS KMS, Google KMS). For HSM-level protections and FIPS endpoints we recommend Private deployments where HSM attachments are supported.
[04:35] Priya: Do you support envelope encryption? We want to keep keys in our KMS and never export raw key material.
[04:42] Liam: Yes, envelope encryption is standard. The model keys remain encrypted and we've got a key-wrapping flow. We'll share the architecture diagram.
[04:54] Sarah: Any crypto certifications? FIPS 140-2/3?
[04:58] Liam: Our hosted endpoints rely on cloud-provider attested HSMs; for Private, you can attach your own FIPS HSM. We'll confirm the provider attestations in the mapping doc.
[05:10] Maya: Quick question on scoping — Priya, which control frameworks do you need mapped? SOC 2 CCs and ISO 27001 Annex A? Anything else?
[05:19] Priya: SOC 2 CCs and ISO Annex A primarily. Also internal control IDs — we'll share a CSV mapping.
[05:27] Asha: From platform perspective, we need to see RBAC APIs, service account lifecycle, and deprovisioning flows.
[05:35] Liam: We'll include API docs and an example of service-account creation/deletion events and the eventual automated deprovisioning policy.
[05:43] Sarah: On SSO — do you support SCIM user provisioning?
[05:46] Liam: Yes, SAML + SCIM for provisioning. Group sync is available so you can map groups to roles.
[05:55] Tom: Are admin actions logged? For example, role changes, key rotations, and export of reports?
[06:02] Liam: Yes, admin actions are captured with actor, timestamp, and the object changed. We'll include a log event schema sample.
[06:12] Priya: For auditability, we need-chain of custody on evidence — who accessed which report and when. Is that available?
[06:21] Liam: Trust Center has access logs for who downloaded or viewed artifacts, and we can export that.
[06:27] Sarah: Great. Regarding controls mapping — can Redwood pre-populate a matrix that maps your controls to SOC 2 and ISO clauses so we can drop in our internal control IDs?
[06:36] Liam: Absolutely. We'll send a pre-filled mapping that shows Redwood control, evidence location (Trust Center link), and how it maps to SOC 2 CC and ISO Annex A. Then you can add Harbor's control IDs.
[06:48] Maya: I'll own coordination on the timeline. We hear May audit window — we'll try to get artifacts by 24th April.
[06:56] Tom: If we get the SOC2 report and the mapping by the 24th, the internal team can tag anything missing quickly.
[07:04] Asha: A couple of nitty gritty questions — tokenization of logs, PII redaction in logs, and prefix caching behavior that might cause data leakage.
[07:14] Liam: Good point — prefix/KV cache is content-agnostic; we ensure cache encryption at rest and lifetime TTLs. We avoid logging prompts unless explicitly enabled; default is to not persist user prompt content. We'll include the default and opt-in logging config.
[07:33] Sarah: That aligns with our data-classification policy. Any options for SIEM integration?
[07:38] Liam: We support log forwarders to Splunk, Sumo, and Elastic. For Private you can point to your own ingest.
[07:46] (short pause)
[08:10] Priya: Can you share the most recent penetration test summary?
[08:15] Maya: We can provide an executive summary; full reports are usually shared under NDA. We can initiate the NDA process if needed.
[08:24] Tom: We'll likely request the full pentest under NDA.
[08:27] Maya: Noted.
[08:40] Liam: On technical certs — I'll double-check the ISO scope statement and whether any subcontractors are excluded. Also will confirm which controls are implemented in our runtime vs infra layer.
[08:55] Sarah: About Trust Center access provisioning — what's the SLA for granting access?
[09:01] Maya: Typically 1 business day once we have your SAML metadata and list of service accounts.
[09:07] Asha: We may want to automate that via SCIM provisioning; is that possible?
[09:12] Liam: SCIM can handle group membership; Trust Center access provisioning still requires an initial mapping but can be automated afterwards.
[09:23] (someone briefly on mute)
[10:00] Tom: Any blockers around sharing the SOC 2 Type II?
[10:03] Maya: No blockers other than NDAs for the full report. Redacted Type II is available via Trust Center.
[10:12] Priya: One more on encryption keys — key rotation cadence and proof of rotation? We need evidence for regular rotation.
[10:20] Liam: Rotation cadence is configurable in KMS. For managed keys we rotate annually by default; for BYOK customers you control rotation. We can provide rotation logs with key version IDs.
[10:33] Sarah: For the mapping doc, include a column for 'evidence filename' and 'Trust Center path' so our auditors can click straight through.
[10:41] Liam: Will do.
[10:50] Maya: Let's recap next steps before we run out of time.
[10:55] Maya: Action items: Maya to send the redacted SOC 2 and ISO cert; Liam to share controls mapping and technical samples; Harbor to send required evidence list and residency zones. We'll target delivery by 2025-04-24.
[11:10] Priya: Sounds good. Also, please include a KMS demo slot — we want the platform team to attend.
[11:16] Liam: I'll schedule a deep dive for the week of May 5.
[11:22] Tom: Any competitors or feature gaps we should be aware of — we've been looking at BigCloudAI for managed endpoints. How do you compare on evidence and control maturity?
[11:32] Maya: We emphasize production predictability and a Trust Center with robust evidence. We'll send a short table comparing typical feature sets; we avoid naming specifics in the doc but can include feature/controls parity notes.
[11:45] Sarah: That helps.
[12:00] (wrap up)
[12:05] Maya: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the artifacts and the calendar invite for the KMS session.
[12:12] Sarah: Thank you.
---
Meeting end.
